newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS to add Copenhagen-Newark flights.
newsitem.headline: SAS to add Copenhagen-Newark flights.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Monday that it planned to start direct flights between Copenhagen and Newark, in the United States, from May 30.

SAS intercontinental routes chief Per Franke told Reuters that the new flight to Newark, nightly except for Mondays and Wednesdays, would increase the carrier's capacity between Scandinavia and the New York area by 30 percent.

Franke added that the new route would be served by Boeing 767 aircraft and he expected it to be profitable, indicating that he expected capacity utilisation above the average for U.S.-bound flights of 70-75 percent.
SAS also plans to introduce a Stockholm-Chicago service, where it expects its alliance with United Airlines to help attract customers.
SAS is jointly owned by the governments of Denmark, Norway and Sweden and by private investors. -- Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom 45 33 96 96 53
